Caveat for the TypeScript half: an integer-valued number is written as an integer there, because JavaScript has no float 2.0; no input here is a float with an integer value.

cases.name: columns that are absent stay absent
a null column stays in the remainder and null in the column
an element without an id is keyed by its position
anonymous keys use the prefix asked for
entries that are not objects are dropped, and z counts only what is kept
a missing or empty type is the empty string
a numeric type is its string
the remainder is json.dumps text: separators, key order, nesting
non-ASCII is escaped as json.dumps escapes it
control characters, quotes, backslashes and DEL
